Lingonberry German 4.0.0 — reviewed study data

Current selected dictionary senses, grammar and primary examples have conversation-agent editorial review with separate source-bound independent component reviews. English and Korean explanations and example translations cover every active entry. No native-speaker certification or official exam endorsement is claimed.

Changes: corrected lexical/translation/grammar/reading data; replaced unsuitable examples; preserved individually attributed licensed material; added original/adapted examples with their component licences; omitted unused private review/history/reference text; assigned new IDs for materially different corrected targets; retired duplicates and unverified teaching targets while preserving existing device history. A1–B1 allocations follow reviewed Goethe headword/sense evidence; B2–C2 remain editorial study bands, not official Goethe word lists.

English, German and Korean Wiktionary contributors retain their per-entry article/history credits and CC BY-SA 4.0 rights. Lingonberry contributors retain original CC BY 4.0 or MIT credits as individually declared; source adaptations keep their declared share-alike licence. Mixed identifiers describe different components, not a relicensing of imported content. Current data and editable JSON: https://github.com/somnio-kimm/lingonberry/tree/main/language-packages

German learner vocabulary 3.0.0 — editorial preview

English, German and Korean Wiktionary contributors are credited for the dictionary facts, definitions and usage examples used by each entry. Source article and contributor-history links are preserved per entry. Extraction: Kaikki/Wiktextract, https://kaikki.org/dictionary/rawdata.html . Adapted content is distributed under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ .

Changes by Learn Language contributors (2026): selected learner headwords; inspected and corrected ambiguous English/Korean sense matches; added original example sentences and translations where suitable reliably translated usage examples were unavailable; assigned study bands; normalised noun display forms; separated study and explanation downloads. New definitions, examples, translations and frequency-based annotations are offered under CC BY-SA 4.0. Original archived MIT material retains its licence below. Local AI assistance was used; no native-speaker review is claimed. This preview needs language review before a production store release.

Goethe-Institut adult A1, A2 and B1 word lists are used only as factual headword/level references. Their publication copyright is not relicensed. No PDF pages or Goethe example sentences are included. Matching uses normalised explicit headwords and thematic groups, not a claim of exhaustive coverage of every productive word family. The earliest matching list determines A1–B1. Unmatched headwords use editorial frequency bands (B2: Zipf >= 4; C1: >= 3; C2: < 3). These upper bands are not official CEFR assessments, exam guarantees or Goethe endorsement.
A1: https://www.goethe.de/pro/relaunch/prf/de/A1_SD1_Wortliste_02.pdf
A2: https://www.goethe.de/pro/relaunch/prf/en/Goethe-Zertifikat_A2_Wortliste.pdf

Wordfreq contains Google Books Ngrams, Leeds Internet Corpus, Wikipedia, ParaCrawl, OpenSubtitles and SUBTLEX-derived statistics; its complete notice follows. It reflects historical usage, not a current CEFR syllabus.

Translation drafts: Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (Apache-2.0), locally run using the mlx-community 4-bit conversion. Model weights and inference libraries are not shipped in the app. Sentence provenance distinguishes source text, original text and model-assisted translation; generated output is not labelled native-speaker reviewed.
